title: Radium-223 (Xofigo)
context_label: Symptomatic bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without known visceral metastases
indication_text: Symptomatic bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without known visceral metastases
purpose: Treat prostate cancer in affected bones, help control symptoms and delay complications in the appropriate disease setting.
schedule_summary: Radium-223 is given as a slow injection into a vein every 28 days, for a maximum of six injections. It is administered by a specialist service authorised to use radioactive medicines.
administration_text: No routine premedication is usually required. The team prescribes sickness or other symptom medicines if needed.
monitoring_summary: Blood count before every injection and four weeks after completion. Baseline kidney/liver tests, bone scan and CT assessment, PSA and testosterone. Assess fracture risk before treatment and monitor bone health for at least 24 months.
safety_note: Call your oncology team immediately for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bleeding or persistent vomiting/diarrhoea. Follow your own temperature and contact plan. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or new leg weakness with bladder/bowel changes: call 112/999.
urgent_extra: Call your oncology team immediately for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bleeding or persistent vomiting/diarrhoea. Follow your own temperature and contact plan. agents.name: Radium-223
agents.mechanism: Radium behaves like calcium and concentrates where bone is being formed around metastases. It emits short-range alpha particles that damage nearby cells. It does not treat visceral metastases and can suppress blood-cell production.
agents.explanation: Radium behaves like calcium and concentrates where bone is being formed around metastases. It emits short-range alpha particles that damage nearby cells. It does not treat visceral metastases and can suppress blood-cell production.
risks: Low blood counts: infection, bleeding, anaemia and possible marrow failure
Bone fractures and worsening bone pain
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site
Jaw-bone problems may occur, particularly with bone-protective medicines
Fertility effects and possible late radiation-related cancer risk; long-term individual risk is uncertain
agents.watch: Do not combine with abiraterone plus prednisone/prednisolone. Bone-protective treatment is assessed before starting. Obtain the nuclear-medicine team’s written toilet, body-fluid, laundry and travel instructions; your treating service will explain which precautions to follow at home and for how long.

anatomy: Call immediately for fever, infection, unusual bruising, bleeding or worsening breathlessness.
Use prescribed support. Persistent vomiting or diarrhoea needs prompt contact.
Drink as advised. Reduced urine, dizziness or inability to drink needs assessment.
Report new focal pain or falls. Discuss bone-protective treatment before starting.
Report jaw pain or a non-healing mouth wound; tell the dentist about all treatments.
Tell staff immediately about pain, burning or swelling around the cannula.
Discuss sperm preservation. Use effective contraception during treatment and for six months afterwards.
New leg weakness or bladder/bowel changes requires emergency assessment.

items.title: How it works
items.text: Radium behaves like calcium and concentrates where bone is being formed around metastases. It emits short-range alpha particles that damage nearby cells. It does not treat visceral metastases and can suppress blood-cell production.

items.title: Radiotherapy
items.text: External-beam radiotherapy may be used for local disease control or symptoms according to the disease setting. Radium-223 is a systemic bone-targeted radiopharmaceutical and is not interchangeable with external-beam treatment.

items.title: Evidence in this setting
items.text: ALSYMPCA studied radium-223 plus best standard care against placebo plus best standard care in symptomatic bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without known visceral metastases. In the updated descriptive analysis of 921 participants, median overall survival was 14.9 versus 11.3 months; hazard ratio 0.695 (95% CI 0.581–0.832). Later safety restrictions and current treatment-selection criteria remain essential; these results do not establish safety with abiraterone or chemotherapy.

evidence.intro: Trial results describe groups and cannot predict an individual outcome.
evidence.population: Symptomatic bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without known visceral metastases
evidence.interpretation: ALSYMPCA studied radium-223 plus best standard care against placebo plus best standard care in symptomatic bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without known visceral metastases. In the updated descriptive analysis of 921 participants, median overall survival was 14.9 versus 11.3 months; hazard ratio 0.695 (95% CI 0.581–0.832). Later safety restrictions and current treatment-selection criteria remain essential; these results do not establish safety with abiraterone or chemotherapy.
limitations: Historical comparisons may not reflect modern previous treatment or available alternatives.
Do not extrapolate outcomes across hormone-sensitive, castration-resistant and nonmetastatic disease.
